label: Double Waistband
note: Owner-uploaded reference images. Authoritative for construction/appearance; NOT usable as the tech-pack illustration (not line art, or shows multiple options).

references.evidence: Sharp 1000x1250 photograph of charcoal flannel high-rise trousers being worn. The waistband is unmistakably TWO stacked tiers divided by a horizontal seam, and each tier carries its own dark 4-hole button (2 buttons stacked vertically on the extension, each with its buttonhole). Also visible: a pointed extension tab, a side-adjuster strap with a silver buckle at the left hip, a belt loop that bridges both tiers, a slanted side pocket, and a single forward pleat falling below the band. This is exactly the stacked-layer, cummerbund-like architecture the label describes.

Photograph (471x705) of navy trousers being worn, same construction: the waistband splits into an upper and a lower tier along a clear horizontal seam, with one 4-hole button on each tier (2 stacked vertically), a pointed tab with a side-adjuster strap and silver buckle at the left hip, a belt loop crossing both tiers, and a single forward pleat below. Light blue shirt above, plain background.

Low-resolution photograph (239x318) of grey high-rise trousers worn outdoors against sand dunes, three-quarter view from the side. The waistband again reads as two tiers separated by a horizontal seam, with two dark buttons stacked vertically, a side-adjuster strap and buckle at the hip, a belt loop and a single forward pleat - but compression softens the tier seam, which is why my confidence is lower than for the other two uploads.
